summary: We developed Derna SAR Flood Monitor, a rapid-response web application designed to monitor and assess flood impacts using Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery. During catastrophic events like the September 2023 floods in Derna, traditional optical satellites are blinded by thick storm clouds and communication blackouts. Our solution addresses this challenge by leveraging all-weather SAR microwave pulses to penetrate clouds and darkness, allowing emergency responders to instantly compare pre- and post-disaster terrain. By quantifying flood-affected areas (0.833 km², 8,327 pixels, 9.25% inundation rate), our platform empowers rescue teams to prioritize high-risk zones and save lives rapidly without dangerous on-ground surveys.
details:
What It Does & How It Works: Derna SAR Flood Monitor is an interactive, open-source web application designed for rapid disaster response and flood impact assessment. Utilizing NASA Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) imagery, the platform detects surface water changes by analyzing radar backscatter drops—penetrating thick storm clouds and total darkness where optical satellites fail. By comparing pre-disaster (August 2023) and post-disaster (September 2023) datasets for Derna, Libya, the system calculates the flood-affected surface area (0.833 km²), water inundation pixels (8,327 pixels), and a 9.25% overall affectation rate, flagging critical triage zones like the Wadi Derna Outlet (-13.2 dB) and Coastal Harbor Basin (-11.1 dB).

Key Benefits & Expected Impact:

  • All-Weather Crisis Monitoring: Eliminates optical blind spots during severe weather and communication blackouts.
  • Interactive Before-and-After Swipe Slider: Enables emergency responders to visually inspect terrain damage instantaneously.
  • Automated JSON Reporting: Generates ready-to-use impact reports to help relief agencies prioritize rescue deployments safely and rapidly.
  • Scalable & Accessible: Supports custom SAR image uploads for future flood events and runs smoothly on both desktop and mobile browsers.

Tools, Languages & Resources Used:

  • Programming Languages: Python, HTML, JavaScript
  • Frameworks & Libraries: Streamlit, Rasterio, NumPy, Matplotlib
  • Data & Hosting: NASA ASF DAAC, Sentinel-1 SAR datasets, GitHub Pages
